Anya — thanks, and great questions. I took the items into a single cover note and attached a short SOW + a pricing workbook for Finance. Key points up front:

- Platform fee (annual): baseline operational/console & control plane fee. This is normally a fixed annual fee tied to the Private control plane subscription. Typical amortization: we can amortize over the committed term in the contract (standard is 12/24/36 months) — i.e., Finance-friendly amortization is supported and documented in the SOW.

- Node licenses: per-GPU/node licensing is metered on a monthly basis and can be combined with a committed node count to create a blended effective unit price. If you commit to N nodes for 12+ months we provide a tiered per-node discount.

- Operator seats: operator licenses are separate. For pilots we include up to 3 operator seats at no charge; production seats are listed in the workbook as a per-seat annual fee (discounted under commit).

- Support tiers: attached spreadsheet outlines three tiers (Standard / SRE / Enterprise). Short summary:
  * Standard: business-hours support, 24h ticket SLA for Sev1, 48h for Sev2. No included on-call.
  * SRE: 24x7 monitoring + 4h response Sev1, 12h Sev2, includes 40 hours annual on-call consulting and 1 escalation call per quarter.
  * Enterprise: 24x7 + guaranteed SRE on-call rotation (dedicated pager), 2h Sev1, 6h Sev2, up to 160 hours/year of on-call and runbook customization; includes agreed credit formula for SLA misses.

- Pilot discount & migration credit: we can offer a 30% pilot discount (3 months, single site) and a one-time migration services credit applied to the first invoice for multi-site rollouts > 6 sites (we typically structure as $Xk credit or 10% of initial implementation fee, whichever is smaller).

I attached: Medivar_SOW_v1.pdf (covers pricing anchors + amortization language) and redwood-support-tiers-2025.xlsx (pricing workbook with line items and examples).

Next steps: I propose a short call tomorrow to walk Finance through row-level numbers. Are you available 10:00–11:00 PT?

Cheers,
